title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 3-5). Grothendieck is building elementary 'tame topology' foundations for topological realisations of networks ('réseaux').

A 'ficelle' (string) is a pair (X,{A,B}) with:
- (a) A, B closed and non-empty (later: 'significantly immersed');
- (b) A ∩ B = ∅;
- (c) (X∖A)/B and (X∖B)/A connected;
- (d) a local irreducibility condition.

Page 3 also gives a variant c′: every connected component of U = X∖(A∪B) has closure meeting both A and B, i.e. 'A and B are the ends of the string'. It reduces to the case where A and B are points by passing to X′ = A\X/B, collapsing A to a and B to b. In that reduced form, (c) says that X′∖{a} and X′∖{b} are connected. The upper-left margin of this page restates exactly this, and notes that a reduced ficelle is connected.

This page defines a 'lieu' (place, cut) of a ficelle. It is a closed C ⊂ X such that either C ∈ {A,B} (the ends themselves), or C ⊂ X∖(A∪B) and condition Li a) holds. Li a) asks for a unique decomposition of X∖C into two disjoint open subspaces U_{A,C} ⊃ A and U_{B,C} ⊃ B with U_{A,C}/A and U_{B,C}/B connected. A first attempt at a condition b), describing C via some union, is struck through.

The bracketed remark and the oblique left margin explain the uniqueness. Passing to X′, the condition means that X′∖C has exactly two connected components, one containing a and one containing b. U_{A,C} and U_{B,C} are then the preimages of these components; Grothendieck writes them as 'the union of the components of X′∖C which contain …'.

The next page builds sub-strings X_{A,C} = closure(U_{A,C}) ∪ C and X_{B,C} likewise. It checks that (X_{A,C},{A,C}) again satisfies a)-c), leaving d) open.

So a lieu is a closed 'level set' cutting the string into two sub-strings: a cut separating the two ends. The evident aim is a linear order on lieux and a cut-and-paste or subdivision calculus for strings, the 1-dimensional 'edge' building block of a network realisation.
errors: Formally the text writes 'C ⊂ {A,B}' where 'C ∈ {A,B}' (C is one of the ends) is meant.
Non-emptiness of C (for C ⊂ X∖(A∪B)) is not stated. With C = ∅, X∖C = X is connected and cannot split into two non-empty disjoint opens, so the definition excludes it anyway.

Uniqueness is asserted, not proved. It does follow: in X′, U′_{A,C} and U′_{B,C} are disjoint connected opens covering X′∖C, so they are exactly its two components. This needs the decomposition to be read in X′, i.e. the connectedness of U_{A,C}/A, as Grothendieck indicates.
Whether collapsing A and B preserves the relevant topology (Hausdorffness, etc.) is tacit. The tame ('modéré') hypotheses mentioned on page 3 presumably cover this.
The ambiguity between X and X′ in 'composantes connexes de X′∖C' is harmless but unresolved on this page.

ideas.what: Ficelle: a space with two disjoint closed ends A, B such that removing one end and collapsing the other leaves a connected space; reduced form X′ with two points a, b, neither of which disconnects X′
ideas.modern_name: Space (continuum) irreducible/connected between two ends; a 'connected cobordism' between A and B; in continuum theory, a continuum in which the end points are non-cut points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Janiszewski, Kuratowski (irreducible continua, 1910s-20s); R.L. Moore and Whyburn (cut-point theory)
ideas.where_published: Not in his published texts as far as known. The Esquisse (1984) announces 'topologie modérée' but contains no such definitions.

ideas.what: Lieu: a closed subset C away from the ends whose complement has exactly two components, one containing each end (after collapsing the ends)
ideas.modern_name: Separator / cut set between a and b; level set of a 'height function'; Kuratowski's layers (tranches) of an irreducible continuum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kuratowski (layers of irreducible continua), Menger/Whyburn (separation theory)

ideas.what: Cutting a string at a lieu C into two sub-strings (closure(U_{A,C}) ∪ C, {A,C}) and (closure(U_{B,C}) ∪ C, {C,B}), worked out on the next page
ideas.modern_name: Subdivision/composition of cobordisms (gluing along a separating hypersurface); order-like structure on separators
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (cobordism categories; Kuratowski's ordering of layers)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'ficelles' and their 'lieux' rebuild, inside his tame-topology programme, essentially Kuratowski's theory of irreducible continua and their ordered layers. Here it is generalised to closed 'ends' A, B and aimed at realising networks. The notes do not cite or connect to the continuum-theory literature. The intended tame setting (where c and c′ coincide and lieux are presumably linearly ordered) is a specific, unexplored use of separation theory as the edge-object of a combinatorial-to-topological realisation functor.
missed.quote: ∃ décomposition de X∖C unique en deux sous-espaces ouverts U_{A,C}, U_{B,C}, A⊂U_{A,C}, B⊂U_{B,C}, U_{A,C}/A et U_{B,C}/B connexes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents how Grothendieck intended to found 'topologie modérée' realisations of réseaux, via an axiomatic 'string' with cut-loci rather than o-minimal cell decomposition. Mathematically, the content is classical.

missed.claim: The local irreducibility condition d) is never shown to pass to sub-strings, and the expected ordering/interval structure on the set of lieux is not established on this page.
missed.quote: Pour que (X_{A,C},{A,C}) soit une ficelle, il ne manque que l'hypothèse d)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. A specialist reconstructing his 1986 tame-topology foundations would need this step; it is likely routine under o-minimal hypotheses.

deep.surprise_reason: These are clean foundational definitions (string with two ends, separating cut-locus, unique two-component splitting) for Grothendieck's tame-topology realisation of networks. They are correct and natural, but essentially classical separation and continuum theory. Their interest is mostly archival: they show the programme in action.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 should read 'ou bien C ∈ {A,B}' (C one of the ends), possibly written ⊂ by slip.
The struck line reads 'Li a) C fermée, et C∈{A,B} ou C⊂U'. A superscript '(X∖(A∪B))', itself partly struck, is written above U at right, explaining U.
The block labelled b) '( C est l'union des retirements … )' is entirely crossed out with large diagonal strokes; it is not a live condition.
Lines 4-5 read 'ou bien les propriétés suivantes sont satisfaites'.

In the bracketed remark, the determined objects are written X_{A,C}, X_{B,C} (not U), 'de façon unique, comme ... l'union des composantes connexes de X′∖C qui contiennent ...'. Under X′ there is a note like 'X/B' or 'X′′', partially struck.
The left oblique margin begins 'i.e. X′∖C a deux composantes connexes ...' and mentions U_A, U_B connected; the overall gist is right.
